c60c68342ac7af7b.question: What does the customer want, and has the bank promised anything so far?

answer.answer: The customer wants her money back: she transferred £4,250 to a 'safe account' after a caller claiming to be Harbourline security told her to move her savings. The file does not record any promise of a refund or reimbursement. The only commitment recorded is that the contact centre agent told her the fraud team would be in touch. That has not happened: no fraud team referral was made, and there was still no owner when the case was chased on 2026-10-21. Under FRD-5, handlers must not promise reimbursement before the specialist decision. The file does not say whether she was asked about support needs. Separately, she has asked for letters in large print.

a247b6cff7aca444.question: Which policy rules decide this case, and what do they require the handler to do?

answer.answer: This is an APP scam: the customer was tricked into a 'safe account' transfer of £4,250. FRD-2 requires handover to Fraud & Scams within 1 business day, and the file shows this has not happened. FRD-3 lists the evidence the handover must contain. FRD-4 requires the account to be secured, which note_1 records. FRD-5 bars promising a refund. CH-6 makes severity High because of the scam and the loss over £1,000. Age, bereavement and low digital skills are VUL-1 indicators, and with bereavement VUL-4 requires referral to Vulnerable Customer Support. VUL-5 means the large-print request must be recorded as an adjustment. The case is Critical with 0 days left, so CH-4 requires a holding letter if no Final Response is sent. The file does not show whether the customer shared security details or was asked about support needs.

Where a customer was tricked into sending a payment to a fraudster, the case must be handed to the Fraud & Scams team within 1 business day.

A fraud or scam handover must include: the date, time and amount of each disputed payment; the payee details as known; how the customer was contacted by the fraudster (if a scam); whether the customer shared any security details; and the date the customer reported it.
On report, the handler must check the account has been secured (cards blocked, online banking credentials reset where needed) and record that this was done.
Card blocked, online banking credentials reset.
